title: Nguyễn lords
capsule: The Nguyễn lords were a feudal clan that governed Đàng Trong (southern Đại Việt) from 1558, when Nguyễn Hoàng—fearing the Trịnh faction at court—secured appointment as governor of the southern marches. Over the following century and a half they waged intermittent warfare against the Trịnh lords of the north, pushing the frontier southward at Champa's and Cambodia's expense and opening southern ports to vigorous trade with European, Japanese, and Chinese merchants. The dynasty reached its territorial apex under Nguyễn Phúc Khoát (r. 1738–1765), who styled himself king. The Tây Sơn uprising swept the lords from power by 1777, massacring nearly the entire family; the sole survivor, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh, spent fifteen years in exile before reconquering the country and founding the Nguyễn imperial dynasty in 1802.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Đàng Trong is moderately well attested through Vietnamese chronicles and European cartography from the 17th–18th centuries, though precise boundary shifts during the Trịnh-Nguyễn wars remain subject to interpretation.
